properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony, 2026-08-09, relayed via dev_storyflow's api-boss: \"If nothing else, we'll see what areas of the graph are not claimed by anyone (orphans). Not sure reflow2 has this feature to detect orphans in ownership.\"

⭐ IT IS A DIFFERENT AXIS FROM orphan_node, AND THE DIFFERENCE IS THE WHOLE POINT.
  orphan_node        structurally disconnected — nothing says what it is FOR.
  ownership orphan   well-connected, realized, verified, SHIPPING — and nobody accountable.

⚠️ A NODE CAN BE STRUCTURALLY PERFECT AND GOVERNANCE-ORPHANED, and that is the more dangerous state precisely because NOTHING ABOUT IT LOOKS WRONG. Every existing detector would pass it: it satisfies a requirement, a component holds it, an artifact realizes it, a check verifies it. The only thing missing is a person, and no detector asks about people.

IT IS ALSO THE THIRD MEMBER OF A FAMILY THIS PROJECT FOUND TWICE TODAY, which is why it is worth naming as a class rather than a feature:
  - req:the-design-says-what-was-built-and-never-used — built, and NOTHING CONSUMES IT.
  - req:a-vocabulary-distinction-proves-it-is-read — declared, and NOTHING READS IT.
  - this one — shipping, and NOBODY OWNS IT.
Every existing gap asks what is MISSING FROM A NODE. All three of these ask what is missing AROUND a node, and none of the seven capability gaps can express that shape.

STRICTLY DEPENDENT ON THE EDGE. There is nothing to detect the absence of until ownership is expressible — dec:idea-ownership-is-the-third-who-axis holds that question. Recorded separately for exactly that reason: the edge can exist without the detector, the detector cannot exist without the edge, and a single node holding both could only be half-answered.

⚠️ THE HARD PART, AND IT IS A DESIGN INPUT RATHER THAN A SETTING — api-boss's, and it is the strongest objection on the table: WHICH NODE TYPES ARE OWNABLE? In their 1,127-node graph most nodes legitimately have no owner; their example is exact — \"a Constraint about prose rendering is nobody's in the accountability sense.\" A naive detector therefore fires on the MAJORITY of a mature graph and becomes a signal trained to be ignored, which is the permanently-red-check failure this project has now written down three times. But in a two-person project the design is probably mostly partitioned, so the same detector is nearly silent and genuinely useful. ⇒ OWNABILITY LOOKS LIKE A PER-PROJECT DECLARATION, NOT A FIXED RULE, and the same feature behaves very differently at those two scales.

THE SHAPES, with counters beside rather than argued down:

(A) A GAP — `unowned_region`, one per ownable node with no owner. Appears in the loop where people already look. COUNTER: the ownability problem above hits this hardest, because a gap that fires on the majority is worse than no gap.

(B) A REPORT — an ownership census: what is owned, by whom, and what is not, reported as a FACT the way granularity_report and surprising_connections are. Cannot nag. COUNTER: a report nobody runs is invisible; it would need a line in graph_report to be seen.

(C) A COVERAGE NUMBER — \"N of M ownable nodes have an owner\", one line, the same shape as the trajectory bands and the certainty line. Cheapest to read, hardest to ignore, and it degrades gracefully at both scales because a low number in a fleet graph is a true statement rather than N nags. COUNTER: a number says nothing about WHICH, so it needs (B) behind it to be actionable.

(D) SCOPED TO A DECLARED PARTITION — a project declares which types are ownable, and the detector only speaks about those. Answers the hard part directly. COUNTER: it is a new declaration to maintain, and an unmaintained one silently narrows the detector to nothing, which is the same class as an unread marker.

⚠️ WHAT MUST NOT HAPPEN, and it is the trap all three of today's findings share: shipping the marker without the computation that reads it, or shipping a computation that fires on correct work. reflow2 has now met the first failure eight times over in its own edge vocabulary and has doctrine against the second in dec:read-hint-shape.

NOTHING IS PROMOTED. Anthony raised the question and said he was not sure the feature existed; it does not.
properties.name: OPEN — should reflow2 detect OWNERSHIP orphans: well-connected, realized, shipping, and nobody accountable?
properties.rationale:
Recorded via the brainstorm skill: `proposed`, options with counters, nothing promoted, and separated from the edge question it depends on so neither can be half-answered.

Worth stating why this one is recorded at all when it cannot be built yet: it is the third instance in one day of a shape reflow2 has no vocabulary for — absence AROUND a node rather than absence IN it — and the other two were captured as intent this session. Recording it keeps the family visible; whether it becomes a fourth requirement is Anthony's call, not a consequence of the first three.
